A debt collector must not engage in any conduct the natural consequence of which is to harass, oppress, or abuse any person in connection with the collection of a debt, including, but not limited to, the conduct described in paragraphs (b) through (h) of this section. (b) Repeated or continuous telephone calls or telephone conversations —(1) In general. In connection with the collection of a debt, a debt collector must not place telephone calls or engage any person in telephone conversation repeatedly or continuously with intent to annoy, abuse, or harass any person at the called number. (2) Telephone call frequencies; presumptions of compliance and violation. (i) Subject to the exclusions in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, a debt collector is presumed to comply with paragraph (b)(1) of this section and FDCPA section 806(5) (15 U.S.C. 1692d(5)) if the debt collector places a telephone call to a particular person in connection with the collection of a particular debt neither: (A) More than seven times within seven consecutive days; nor (B) Within a period of seven consecutive days after having had a telephone conversation with the person in connection with the collection of such debt. The date of the telephone conversation is the first day of the seven-consecutive-day period. (ii) Subject to the exclusions in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, a debt collector is presumed to violate paragraph (b)(1) of this section and FDCPA section 806(5) if the debt collector places a telephone call to a particular person in connection with the collection of a particular debt in excess of either of the telephone call frequencies described in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section. (a) In general. (b) Collection of unauthorized amounts. A debt collector must not collect any amount unless such amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law. A debt collector must not: (1) Accept from any person a check or other payment instrument postdated by more than five days unless such person is notified in writing of the debt collector's intent to deposit such check or instrument not more than ten, nor less than three, days (excluding legal public holidays identified in 5 U.S.C. 6103(a), Saturdays, and Sundays) prior to such deposit. (2) Solicit any postdated check or other postdated payment instrument for the purpose of threatening or instituting criminal prosecution. (a) Definition. For purposes of this section, the term consumer includes: (1) The consumer's spouse; (2) The consumer's parent, if the consumer is a minor; (3) The consumer's legal guardian; (4) The executor or administrator of the consumer's estate, if the consumer is deceased; and (5) A confirmed successor in interest, as defined in Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024.31, or Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(27)(ii). (b) Communications with a consumer —(1) Prohibitions regarding unusual or inconvenient times or places. Except as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section, a debt collector must not communicate or attempt to communicate with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt: (i) At any unusual time, or at a time that the debt collector knows or should know is inconvenient to the consumer. In the absence of the debt collector's knowledge of circumstances to the contrary, a time before 8:00 a.m. and after 9:00 p.m. local time at the consumer's location is inconvenient; or (ii) At any unusual place, or at a place that the debt collector knows or should know is inconvenient to the consumer. (2) Prohibitions regarding consumer represented by an attorney. Except as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section, a debt collector must not communicate or attempt to communicate with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt if the debt collector knows the consumer is represented by an attorney with respect to such debt and knows, or can readily ascertain, the attorney's name and address, unless the attorney: (i) Fails to respond within a reasonable period of time to a communication from the debt collector; or (ii) Consents to the debt collector's direct communication with the consumer. (3) Prohibitions regarding consumer's place of employment. Except as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section, a debt collector must not communicate or attempt to communicate with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt at the consumer's place of employment, if the debt collector knows or has reason to know that the consumer's employer prohibits the consumer from receiving such communication. (4) Exceptions. The prohibitions in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section do not apply when a debt collector communicates or attempts to communicate with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt with: (i) The prior consent of the consumer, given directly to the debt collector during a communication that does not violate paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section; or (ii) The express permission of a court of competent jurisdiction. (c) Communications with a consumer—after refusal to pay or cease communication notice —(1) Prohibition.

(a) Definition. The term location information means a consumer's: (1) Place of abode and telephone number at such place; or (2) Place of employment. (b) Form and content of location communications. A debt collector communicating with a person other than the consumer for the purpose of acquiring location information must: (1) Identify himself or herself individually by name, state that he or she is confirming or correcting the consumer's location information, and, only if expressly requested, identify his or her employer; (2) Not state that the consumer owes any debt; (3) Not communicate by postcard; (4) Not use any language or symbol on any envelope or in the contents of any communication by mail indicating that the debt collector is in the debt collection business or that the communication relates to the collection of a debt; and (5) After the debt collector knows the consumer is represented by an attorney with regard to the subject debt and has knowledge of, or can readily ascertain, such attorney's name and address, not communicate with any person other than that attorney, unless the attorney fails to respond to the debt collector's communication within a reasonable period of time. (c) Frequency of location communications. In addition to complying with § 1006.14(b)(1), a debt collector communicating with any person other than the consumer for the purpose of acquiring location information about the consumer must not communicate more than once with such person unless requested to do so by such person, or unless the debt collector reasonably believes that the earlier response of such person is erroneous or incomplete and that such person now has correct or complete location information.

CFPB Consumer Laws and Regulations FDCPA Unfair Practices – 15 U.S.C. 1692f A debt collector may not use unfair or unconscionable means to collect or attempt to collect a debt. For example, a debt collector may not: • Collect any interest, fee, charge, or expense incidental to the principal obligation unless it was authorized by the original debt agreement or is otherwise permitted by law. • Accept a check or other instrument post-dated by more than five days, unless he or she notifies the consumer, in writing, of any intention to deposit the check or instrument. That notice must be made not more than ten or less than three business days before the date of deposit. • Solicit a post-dated check or other post-dated payment instrument to use as a threat or to institute criminal prosecution. • Deposit or threaten to deposit a post-dated check or other post-dated payment instrument before the date on the check or instrument. • Cause communication charges, such as those for collect telephone calls and telegrams, to be made to any person by concealing the true purpose of the communication. • Take or threaten to repossess or disable property when the creditor has no enforceable right to the property or does not intend to do so, or if, under law, the property cannot be taken, repossessed, or disabled. • Use a postcard to contact a consumer about a debt. • Use any language or symbol, other than the debt collector’s address, on any envelope when communicating with a consumer; a debt collector may use its business name if such name does not indicate it is in the debt collection business. Multiple Debts – 15 U.S.C. 1692h If a consumer owes several debts that are being collected by the same debt collector, payments must be applied according to the consumer’s instructions. No payment may be applied to a disputed debt. Legal Actions By Debt Collectors – 15 U.S.C. 1692i A debt collector may file a lawsuit to enforce a security interest in real property only in the judicial district in which the real property is located. Other legal actions may be brought only in the judicial district in which the consumer lives or in which the original contract creating the debt was signed. Furnishing Certain Deceptive Forms – 15 U.S.C. 1692j No one may design, compile and/or furnish any form that creates the false impression that someone other than the creditor (for example, a debt collector) is participating in the collection of a debt. ## Restrictions on Frequency and Timing of Telephone Calls by Debt Collectors

### 1. Timing Restrictions

A debt collector must not communicate or attempt to communicate with a consumer:

- **At any unusual time**, or at a time the debt collector knows or should know is inconvenient to the consumer
- Specifically, **before 8:00 a.m. or after 9:00 p.m. local time** at the consumer's location is presumed inconvenient in the absence of knowledge of circumstances to the contrary [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001]

### 2. Frequency Restrictions

A debt collector must not place telephone calls **repeatedly or continuously with intent to annoy, abuse, or harass** any person at the called number [C:12CFR1006_1006.14_chunk_0001].

#### Safe Harbor (Presumption of Compliance)
A debt collector is **presumed to comply** with the harassment prohibition if calls to a particular person regarding a particular debt are placed:
- **No more than seven times within seven consecutive days**, AND
- **Not within seven consecutive days after having had a telephone conversation** with the person about that debt (the date of the conversation counts as day one of that period) [C:12CFR1006_1006.14_chunk_0001]

#### Presumption of Violation
Conversely, exceeding these thresholds creates a **presumption of violation** of the harassment prohibition [C:12CFR1006_1006.14_chunk_0001].

### 3. Additional Restrictions

- A debt collector must **not place calls without meaningfully disclosing the caller's identity** [C:12CFR1006_1006.14_chunk_0002]
- If the consumer is **represented by an attorney**, the debt collector must not communicate directly with the consumer [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001]
- When contacting **third parties for location information**, the debt collector must not contact such persons more than once [C:12CFR1006_1006.10_chunk_0001]

### Summary Table

| Restriction | Rule |
|---|---|
| Earliest call time | 8:00 a.m. local time |
| Latest call time | 9:00 p.m. local time |
| Max calls per 7-day period | 7 calls per debt |
| Calls after a conversation | None for 7 consecutive days |

answer:
## Debt Collector Communication Rules: Timing, Location, and Restrictions

### 1. Definition of "Consumer"

For communication purposes, "consumer" is broadly defined to include not just the debtor, but also:
- The consumer's spouse
- The consumer's parent (if the consumer is a minor)
- The consumer's legal guardian
- The executor or administrator of the consumer's estate (if deceased)
- A confirmed successor in interest [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001]

---

### 2. Prohibited Times for Communication

A debt collector **must not** communicate with a consumer at any **unusual time** or at a time the debt collector **knows or should know is inconvenient**. [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001]

**Default presumption of inconvenience:**
> Before **8:00 a.m.** and after **9:00 p.m.** local time at the consumer's location is presumed inconvenient, absent knowledge of circumstances to the contrary. [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0668_chunk_0001]

---

### 3. Prohibited Places for Communication

A debt collector must not communicate at any **unusual place** or a place the collector **knows or should know is inconvenient** to the consumer. [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001]

Additionally, a debt collector **may not contact the consumer at their place of employment** if the collector has reason to believe the employer prohibits such communications. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0668_chunk_0001]

---

### 4. Prohibition When Consumer Has an Attorney

A debt collector must not communicate with a consumer if the debt collector:
- Knows the consumer is **represented by an attorney** with respect to the debt, **and**
- Knows or can readily ascertain the attorney's contact information [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0668_chunk_0001]

---

### 5. Exceptions Permitting Otherwise Prohibited Communications

Despite the above restrictions, communication **is permitted** if made with:
1. **The prior consent of the consumer**, given directly to the debt collector during a communication that does not itself violate the prohibitions; or
2. **The express permission of a court of competent jurisdiction** [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0002]

---

### 6. Cease Communication Rules

If a consumer **notifies the debt collector in writing** that they refuse to pay or want communication to cease, the debt collector **must stop all further communication**. [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0002]

**Narrow exceptions** allow further contact only to:
- Advise the consumer that the debt collector's efforts are being terminated
- Notify the consumer that the debt collector or creditor **may invoke specified remedies**
- Notify the consumer that the debt collector or creditor **intends to invoke a specified remedy** [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0002]

---

### Summary Table

| Rule | Requirement |
|------|-------------|
| Time restriction | No contact before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. (consumer's local time) |
| Place restriction | No contact at unusual or known-inconvenient locations |
| Workplace | No contact if employer prohibits it |
| Attorney representation | No direct consumer contact if attorney is known |
| Exceptions | Consumer consent or court permission |
| Cease communication | Must stop upon written notice, with only three narrow exceptions |

## Debt Collector Communication Rules: Timing, Location, and Restrictions

### 1. Definition of "Consumer"

For communication purposes, "consumer" is broadly defined to include not just the debtor, but also:
- The consumer's spouse
- The consumer's parent (if the consumer is a minor)
- The consumer's legal guardian
- The executor or administrator of the consumer's estate (if deceased)
- A confirmed successor in interest [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001]

---

### 2. Prohibited Times for Communication

A debt collector **must not** communicate with a consumer at any **unusual time** or at a time the debt collector **knows or should know is inconvenient**. [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001]

**Default presumption of inconvenience:**
> Before **8:00 a.m.** and after **9:00 p.m.** local time at the consumer's location is presumed inconvenient, absent knowledge of circumstances to the contrary. [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0668_chunk_0001]

---

### 3. Prohibited Places for Communication

A debt collector must not communicate at any **unusual place** or a place the collector **knows or should know is inconvenient** to the consumer. [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001]

Additionally, a debt collector **may not contact the consumer at their place of employment** if the collector has reason to believe the employer prohibits such communications. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0668_chunk_0001]

---

### 4. Prohibition When Consumer Has an Attorney

A debt collector must not communicate with a consumer if the debt collector:
- Knows the consumer is **represented by an attorney** with respect to the debt, **and**
- Knows or can readily ascertain the attorney's contact information [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0668_chunk_0001]

---

### 5. Exceptions Permitting Otherwise Prohibited Communications

Despite the above restrictions, communication **is permitted** if made with:
1. **The prior consent of the consumer**, given directly to the debt collector during a communication that does not itself violate the prohibitions; or
2. **The express permission of a court of competent jurisdiction** [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0002]

---

### 6. Cease Communication Rules

If a consumer **notifies the debt collector in writing** that they refuse to pay or want communication to cease, the debt collector **must stop all further communication**. [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0002]

**Narrow exceptions** allow further contact only to:
- Advise the consumer that the debt collector's efforts are being terminated
- Notify the consumer that the debt collector or creditor **may invoke specified remedies**
- Notify the consumer that the debt collector or creditor **intends to invoke a specified remedy** [C:12CFR1006_1006.6_chunk_0002]

---

### Summary Table

| Rule | Requirement |
|------|-------------|
| Time restriction | No contact before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. (consumer's local time) |
| Place restriction | No contact at unusual or known-inconvenient locations |
| Workplace | No contact if employer prohibits it |
| Attorney representation | No direct consumer contact if attorney is known |
| Exceptions | Consumer consent or court permission |
| Cease communication | Must stop upon written notice, with only three narrow exceptions |

question: What information must a debt collector provide in a validation notice, and when must it be sent?
answer:
## Validation Notice Requirements Under 12 CFR 1006.34

### When Must It Be Sent?

A debt collector must provide validation information to a consumer either:

- **In the initial communication** itself, or
- **Within five days** of the initial communication [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0001]

This may be delivered as a written/electronic validation notice or **orally** during the initial communication [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0001].

> **Exception:** If the consumer pays the debt before the five-day deadline would require the notice to be sent, the debt collector is not required to send it [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0001].

---

### What Information Must Be Included?

#### 1. Debt Collector Communication Disclosure
The statement required by § 1006.18(e) [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0002].

#### 2. Information About the Debt
- The **debt collector's name and mailing address** for disputes and original-creditor requests
- The **consumer's name and mailing address**
- The **name of the creditor** to whom the debt was owed on the itemization date (for consumer financial product/service debts)
- The **account number**, if any, associated with the debt on the itemization date [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0002]

#### 3. Validation Period Information
- The **end date of the validation period** and notice that the consumer may dispute the debt in writing by that date, triggering the debt collector's obligation to cease collection until verification is provided
- The end date and notice that the consumer may **request the original creditor's name and address** in writing by that date
- A statement that unless the consumer disputes the debt by that date, the **debt collector will assume the debt is valid**
- For consumer financial product/service debts, a statement directing the consumer to **www.cfpb.gov/debt-collection** for additional consumer protection information [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0003]

#### 4. Electronic Communication Information (if applicable)
If the notice is sent electronically:
- The debt collector's **website and email address**
- If the validation information is *not* provided electronically, a statement explaining how the consumer can dispute the debt or request original-creditor information electronically [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0006]

#### 5. Spanish-Language Disclosures (Optional but Regulated)
A debt collector *may* include either or both of the following:
- The Spanish statement **"Póngase en contacto con nosotros para solicitar una copia de este formulario en español"**
- The Spanish prompt **"Quiero este formulario en español"** next to a consumer-response prompt [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0006]

If a debt collector includes these optional disclosures and the consumer subsequently requests a Spanish-language notice, the debt collector **must** provide a fully translated Spanish validation notice [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0007].

---

### Validation Period Definition

The validation period begins when the debt collector provides the validation information and ends **30 days after the consumer receives or is assumed to receive it**. The debt collector may assume receipt occurs at least **five days** (excluding legal public holidays, Saturdays, and Sundays) after sending [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0002].

---

### Form Requirements

All validation information must be **clear and conspicuous** — readily understandable, noticeable, and legible [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0004]. A **safe harbor** is available to debt collectors who use **Model Form B-1** or a substantially similar variation [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0004].

---

### Special Rule for Residential Mortgage Debt

For residential mortgage debt subject to Regulation Z periodic statement requirements, a debt collector need not provide certain itemization information if it provides the consumer with a **copy of the most recent periodic statement** in the same communication [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0004].

## Validation Notice Requirements Under 12 CFR 1006.34

### When Must It Be Sent?

A debt collector must provide validation information to a consumer either:

- **In the initial communication** itself, or
- **Within five days** of the initial communication [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0001]

This may be delivered as a written/electronic validation notice or **orally** during the initial communication [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0001].

> **Exception:** If the consumer pays the debt before the five-day deadline would require the notice to be sent, the debt collector is not required to send it [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0001].

---

### What Information Must Be Included?

#### 1. Debt Collector Communication Disclosure
The statement required by § 1006.18(e) [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0002].

#### 2. Information About the Debt
- The **debt collector's name and mailing address** for disputes and original-creditor requests
- The **consumer's name and mailing address**
- The **name of the creditor** to whom the debt was owed on the itemization date (for consumer financial product/service debts)
- The **account number**, if any, associated with the debt on the itemization date [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0002]

#### 3. Validation Period Information
- The **end date of the validation period** and notice that the consumer may dispute the debt in writing by that date, triggering the debt collector's obligation to cease collection until verification is provided
- The end date and notice that the consumer may **request the original creditor's name and address** in writing by that date
- A statement that unless the consumer disputes the debt by that date, the **debt collector will assume the debt is valid**
- For consumer financial product/service debts, a statement directing the consumer to **www.cfpb.gov/debt-collection** for additional consumer protection information [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0003]

#### 4. Electronic Communication Information (if applicable)
If the notice is sent electronically:
- The debt collector's **website and email address**
- If the validation information is *not* provided electronically, a statement explaining how the consumer can dispute the debt or request original-creditor information electronically [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0006]

#### 5. Spanish-Language Disclosures (Optional but Regulated)
A debt collector *may* include either or both of the following:
- The Spanish statement **"Póngase en contacto con nosotros para solicitar una copia de este formulario en español"**
- The Spanish prompt **"Quiero este formulario en español"** next to a consumer-response prompt [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0006]

If a debt collector includes these optional disclosures and the consumer subsequently requests a Spanish-language notice, the debt collector **must** provide a fully translated Spanish validation notice [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0007].

---

### Validation Period Definition

The validation period begins when the debt collector provides the validation information and ends **30 days after the consumer receives or is assumed to receive it**. The debt collector may assume receipt occurs at least **five days** (excluding legal public holidays, Saturdays, and Sundays) after sending [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0002].

---

### Form Requirements

All validation information must be **clear and conspicuous** — readily understandable, noticeable, and legible [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0004]. A **safe harbor** is available to debt collectors who use **Model Form B-1** or a substantially similar variation [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0004].

---

### Special Rule for Residential Mortgage Debt

For residential mortgage debt subject to Regulation Z periodic statement requirements, a debt collector need not provide certain itemization information if it provides the consumer with a **copy of the most recent periodic statement** in the same communication [C:12CFR1006_1006.34_chunk_0004].

question: What account-opening disclosures must a depository institution provide under Regulation DD?
answer:
## Account-Opening Disclosures Under Regulation DD

### Statutory Purpose

Regulation DD (12 CFR Part 1030) implements the Truth in Savings Act (TISA) and is designed **"to enable consumers to make informed decisions about their accounts at depository institutions through the use of uniform disclosures."** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0746_chunk_0001]

---

### Timing of Account-Opening Disclosures (12 CFR 1030.4(a)(1))

Depository institutions must provide disclosures according to the following timing rules:

| Scenario | Requirement |
|----------|-------------|
| Consumer present at account opening | Disclosures provided **before** account is opened or service provided, whichever is earlier |
| Consumer **not present** at opening | Mail or deliver disclosures **no later than 10 business days** after account is opened or service provided |
| Consumer uses **electronic means** (e.g., website) to open account | Disclosures must be provided **before** the account is opened or service is provided |

[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0783_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0797_chunk_0001]

---

### Disclosures Upon Request (12 CFR 1030.4(a)(2))

- Institutions must provide **full account disclosures, including complete fee schedules**, to any consumer upon request — whether an existing or prospective customer [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001]
- An oral inquiry about rates, yields, or fees does **not** trigger the duty to provide written disclosures [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001]
- When written information is requested **in person**, disclosures must be provided **at that time** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001]
- When the request is **not made in person**, disclosures must be mailed or delivered within a **reasonable time** (10 business days is considered reasonable) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001]

---

### Format Requirements for Disclosures

Disclosures must be [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0751_chunk_0001]:

- **In a form the consumer may keep**
- **Clearly identifiable** for different accounts if combined
- **Reflective of the terms** of the legal obligation in the account agreement
- **Available in English** upon request if provided in another language
- **Consistent in terminology** when describing required terms or features

---

### Electronic Disclosures

Regulation DD disclosures **may** be provided electronically, subject to compliance with the **E-Sign Act** (15 U.S.C. § 7001 et seq.). Before consent is given, the institution must inform the consumer of:

- Any right to receive information in **paper or non-electronic form**
- The right to **withdraw consent** to receive electronic disclosures

[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0751_chunk_0001]

---

### Coverage Note

Regulation DD applies to all depository institutions **except credit unions** that offer deposit accounts to consumers, including U.S. branches of foreign institutions. Edge Act corporations and agencies of foreign institutions are **not** covered. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0747_chunk_0001]

---

### Accuracy of Advertised Terms

Institutions must ensure that advertised account terms (such as bonuses) are accurate and not misleading. Failure to honor advertised bonus offers to eligible consumers has been found to violate Regulation DD. [C:sh_issue22_2020-09_page_0011_chunk_0001]

evidence.text: CFPB Consumer Laws and Regulations TISA The regulation also includes requirements on the payment of interest, the methods of calculating the balance on which interest is paid, the calculation of the annual-percentage yield, and advertising. Coverage – 12 CFR 1030.1 Regulation DD applies to all depository institutions, except credit unions, that offer deposit accounts to residents of any state. Branches of foreign institutions located in the United States are subject to Regulation DD if they offer deposit accounts to consumers. Edge Act and agreement corporations, and agencies of foreign institutions, are not depository institutions for purposes of Regulation DD. In addition, persons who advertise accounts are subject to the advertising rules. For example, if a deposit broker places an advertisement offering consumers an account at a depository institution, the advertising rules apply to the advertisement, whether the account is to be held by the broker or directly by the consumer. Definitions – 12 CFR 1030.2 Section 1030.2 defines key terms used in Regulation DD. Among those definitions are the following: Account – 12 CFR 1030.2(a) An account is a deposit account at a depository institution that is held by or offered to a consumer. ## Account-Opening Disclosures Under Regulation DD

### Statutory Purpose

Regulation DD (12 CFR Part 1030) implements the Truth in Savings Act (TISA) and is designed **"to enable consumers to make informed decisions about their accounts at depository institutions through the use of uniform disclosures."** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0746_chunk_0001]

---

### Timing of Account-Opening Disclosures (12 CFR 1030.4(a)(1))

Depository institutions must provide disclosures according to the following timing rules:

| Scenario | Requirement |
|----------|-------------|
| Consumer present at account opening | Disclosures provided **before** account is opened or service provided, whichever is earlier |
| Consumer **not present** at opening | Mail or deliver disclosures **no later than 10 business days** after account is opened or service provided |
| Consumer uses **electronic means** (e.g., website) to open account | Disclosures must be provided **before** the account is opened or service is provided |

[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0783_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0797_chunk_0001]

---

### Disclosures Upon Request (12 CFR 1030.4(a)(2))

- Institutions must provide **full account disclosures, including complete fee schedules**, to any consumer upon request — whether an existing or prospective customer [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001]
- An oral inquiry about rates, yields, or fees does **not** trigger the duty to provide written disclosures [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001]
- When written information is requested **in person**, disclosures must be provided **at that time** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001]
- When the request is **not made in person**, disclosures must be mailed or delivered within a **reasonable time** (10 business days is considered reasonable) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0754_chunk_0001]

---

### Format Requirements for Disclosures

Disclosures must be [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0751_chunk_0001]:

- **In a form the consumer may keep**
- **Clearly identifiable** for different accounts if combined
- **Reflective of the terms** of the legal obligation in the account agreement
- **Available in English** upon request if provided in another language
- **Consistent in terminology** when describing required terms or features

---

### Electronic Disclosures

Regulation DD disclosures **may** be provided electronically, subject to compliance with the **E-Sign Act** (15 U.S.C. § 7001 et seq.). Before consent is given, the institution must inform the consumer of:

- Any right to receive information in **paper or non-electronic form**
- The right to **withdraw consent** to receive electronic disclosures

[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0751_chunk_0001]

---

### Coverage Note

Regulation DD applies to all depository institutions **except credit unions** that offer deposit accounts to consumers, including U.S. branches of foreign institutions. Edge Act corporations and agencies of foreign institutions are **not** covered. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0747_chunk_0001]

---

### Accuracy of Advertised Terms

Institutions must ensure that advertised account terms (such as bonuses) are accurate and not misleading. Failure to honor advertised bonus offers to eligible consumers has been found to violate Regulation DD. [C:sh_issue22_2020-09_page_0011_chunk_0001]

question: What rules govern the payment of interest on interest-bearing deposit accounts?
answer:
## Rules Governing Payment of Interest on Interest-Bearing Deposit Accounts

The Truth in Savings Act (TISA) and its implementing regulation, Regulation DD (12 CFR Part 1030), establish the following rules:

---

### 1. Balance Calculation Methods

Institutions must calculate interest based on the **full amount of principal** in an account each day, using either:
- The **daily balance method**, or
- The **average daily balance method**

[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001]

---

### 2. Minimum Balance Requirements

- If an institution requires a minimum balance to earn interest, it **must use the same method** to determine the required minimum balance as it uses to calculate interest [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001].
- An institution **may** use an additional method only if it is **unequivocally beneficial** to the consumer [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001].
- If the balance drops below the required minimum, the institution **may choose not to pay interest** for those days [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001].
- Institutions **must pay interest on the full balance** that meets the minimum — for example, if the minimum is $300 and a consumer deposits $500, interest must be paid on the full $500 [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001].

---

### 3. When Interest Begins to Accrue

Interest **must begin to accrue no later than the business day** on which the depository institution receives **provisional credit** for deposited funds, as required by Section 606 of the Expedited Funds Availability Act and Regulation CC [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0766_chunk_0001].

---

### 4. When Interest Stops Accruing

Interest **accrues until the day funds are withdrawn** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0766_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0804_chunk_0001].

---

### 5. Compounding and Crediting Frequency

- An institution is **not required** to compound or credit interest at any particular frequency.
- However, if it does, it may do so **annually, semi-annually, quarterly, monthly, daily, continuously, or on any other basis** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0804_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

---

### 6. Early Account Closure

- If an institution chooses **not to pay accrued interest** when a consumer closes an account **prior to the date accrued interest is credited**, it **must disclose this practice** in the initial account disclosures [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0804_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

---

### 7. Definition of Interest

For regulatory purposes, **interest** means any payment to a consumer or to an account for the use of funds, calculated by applying a periodic rate to the balance. It does **not** include:
- Bonuses or other consideration worth **$10 or less** during a year,
- The waiver or reduction of a fee, or
- The absorption of expenses

[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0749_chunk_0001]

## Rules Governing Payment of Interest on Interest-Bearing Deposit Accounts

The Truth in Savings Act (TISA) and its implementing regulation, Regulation DD (12 CFR Part 1030), establish the following rules:

---

### 1. Balance Calculation Methods

Institutions must calculate interest based on the **full amount of principal** in an account each day, using either:
- The **daily balance method**, or
- The **average daily balance method**

[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001]

---

### 2. Minimum Balance Requirements

- If an institution requires a minimum balance to earn interest, it **must use the same method** to determine the required minimum balance as it uses to calculate interest [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001].
- An institution **may** use an additional method only if it is **unequivocally beneficial** to the consumer [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001].
- If the balance drops below the required minimum, the institution **may choose not to pay interest** for those days [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001].
- Institutions **must pay interest on the full balance** that meets the minimum — for example, if the minimum is $300 and a consumer deposits $500, interest must be paid on the full $500 [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001].

---

### 3. When Interest Begins to Accrue

Interest **must begin to accrue no later than the business day** on which the depository institution receives **provisional credit** for deposited funds, as required by Section 606 of the Expedited Funds Availability Act and Regulation CC [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0766_chunk_0001].

---

### 4. When Interest Stops Accruing

Interest **accrues until the day funds are withdrawn** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0766_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0804_chunk_0001].

---

### 5. Compounding and Crediting Frequency

- An institution is **not required** to compound or credit interest at any particular frequency.
- However, if it does, it may do so **annually, semi-annually, quarterly, monthly, daily, continuously, or on any other basis** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0804_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

---

### 6. Early Account Closure

- If an institution chooses **not to pay accrued interest** when a consumer closes an account **prior to the date accrued interest is credited**, it **must disclose this practice** in the initial account disclosures [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0804_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

---

### 7. Definition of Interest

For regulatory purposes, **interest** means any payment to a consumer or to an account for the use of funds, calculated by applying a periodic rate to the balance. It does **not** include:
- Bonuses or other consideration worth **$10 or less** during a year,
- The waiver or reduction of a fee, or
- The absorption of expenses

[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0749_chunk_0001]

question: What requirements apply to the calculation of interest on deposit accounts?
answer:
## Requirements for Calculating Interest on Deposit Accounts

### Permissible Balance Calculation Methods

Under 12 CFR 1030.7(a)(1), an institution **must** calculate interest on the full amount of principal in an account for each day using one of two permitted methods [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0764_chunk_0001]:

1. **Daily Balance Method** – The daily periodic rate is applied to the full amount of principal in the account each day.
2. **Average Daily Balance Method** – A periodic rate is applied to the average daily balance, calculated by adding the full amount of principal for each day of the period and dividing by the number of days in the period.

### Prohibited Methods

The following methods are explicitly **prohibited** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0764_chunk_0001]:
- **Ending-balance method** – paying interest only on the balance at end of period
- **Low-balance method** – paying interest based on the lowest balance during the period
- **Investable-balance method** – paying interest on only a percentage of the balance, excluding reserves

---

### Minimum Balance Consistency Requirement

For accounts requiring a minimum balance to earn interest, the institution must use the **same method** to determine the minimum balance as it uses to determine the balance on which interest is calculated. An institution may use an additional method only if it is **unequivocally beneficial to the consumer** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

---

### Day-Count and Rate Application Rules

- Institutions may apply a daily periodic rate greater than 1/365 of the interest rate (e.g., 1/360), **as long as it is applied 365 days a year** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0764_chunk_0001].
- In a **leap year**, institutions may apply a daily rate of either 1/366 or 1/365 of the interest rate for 366 days [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0764_chunk_0001].

---

### Compounding and Crediting

An institution is **not required** to compound or credit interest at any particular frequency, but if it does, it may do so annually, semi-annually, quarterly, monthly, daily, continuously, or on any other basis [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

If an institution chooses **not to pay accrued interest** when a consumer closes an account before the crediting date, it must **disclose this practice** in the initial account disclosures [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

---

### Disclosure Requirements Related to Interest

Institutions must disclose both the **annual percentage yield (APY)** and the **interest rate** using those exact terms, along with compounding and crediting frequency [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0755_chunk_0001]. The interest rate is defined as the annual rate paid on an account and does **not** reflect compounding [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0749_chunk_0001].

## Requirements for Calculating Interest on Deposit Accounts

### Permissible Balance Calculation Methods

Under 12 CFR 1030.7(a)(1), an institution **must** calculate interest on the full amount of principal in an account for each day using one of two permitted methods [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0764_chunk_0001]:

1. **Daily Balance Method** – The daily periodic rate is applied to the full amount of principal in the account each day.
2. **Average Daily Balance Method** – A periodic rate is applied to the average daily balance, calculated by adding the full amount of principal for each day of the period and dividing by the number of days in the period.

### Prohibited Methods

The following methods are explicitly **prohibited** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0764_chunk_0001]:
- **Ending-balance method** – paying interest only on the balance at end of period
- **Low-balance method** – paying interest based on the lowest balance during the period
- **Investable-balance method** – paying interest on only a percentage of the balance, excluding reserves

---

### Minimum Balance Consistency Requirement

For accounts requiring a minimum balance to earn interest, the institution must use the **same method** to determine the minimum balance as it uses to determine the balance on which interest is calculated. An institution may use an additional method only if it is **unequivocally beneficial to the consumer** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

---

### Day-Count and Rate Application Rules

- Institutions may apply a daily periodic rate greater than 1/365 of the interest rate (e.g., 1/360), **as long as it is applied 365 days a year** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0764_chunk_0001].
- In a **leap year**, institutions may apply a daily rate of either 1/366 or 1/365 of the interest rate for 366 days [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0764_chunk_0001].

---

### Compounding and Crediting

An institution is **not required** to compound or credit interest at any particular frequency, but if it does, it may do so annually, semi-annually, quarterly, monthly, daily, continuously, or on any other basis [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

If an institution chooses **not to pay accrued interest** when a consumer closes an account before the crediting date, it must **disclose this practice** in the initial account disclosures [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

---

### Disclosure Requirements Related to Interest

Institutions must disclose both the **annual percentage yield (APY)** and the **interest rate** using those exact terms, along with compounding and crediting frequency [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0755_chunk_0001]. The interest rate is defined as the annual rate paid on an account and does **not** reflect compounding [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0749_chunk_0001].

## Deposit Account Compliance Findings in CFPB Supervisory Highlights

### Coverage of Deposit Accounts in the Corpus

The evidence confirms that deposit accounts were examined and findings were included in at least two issues of Supervisory Highlights:

- **Issue 18 (Winter 2019)** covered examinations "in the areas of automobile loan servicing, **deposits**, mortgage servicing, and remittances that were generally completed between June and November 2018" [C:sh_issue18_2019-03_page_0003_chunk_0001]

- **Issue 22 (Summer 2020)** covered examinations "in the areas of consumer reporting, debt collection, **deposits**, fair lending, and mortgage servicing that were completed between September 2019 and December 2019" [C:sh_issue22_2020-09_page_0003_chunk_0001]

### Limitation of Available Evidence

**The corpus does not contain the substantive deposit-account findings sections** from either of these issues. While the introductory pages confirm that deposit-related examination findings exist in Issues 18 and 22, the actual chunks describing specific violations, practices, or compliance deficiencies in deposit accounts are not present in the provided evidence.

The evidence available covers only:
- Introductory/scope language [C:sh_issue18_2019-03_page_0003_chunk_0001; C:sh_issue22_2020-09_page_0003_chunk_0001]
- Conclusion sections [C:sh_issue18_2019-03_page_0021_chunk_0001; C:sh_issue23_2021-01_page_0028_chunk_0001]
- Supervisory communication procedural guidance [C:sh_issue18_2019-03_page_0018_chunk_0001]
- Examination report templates [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0911_chunk_0001; C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0923_chunk_0001]

### What Can Be Said Generally

Based on the procedural framework described, any deposit-account findings would have been communicated as either:
- **Matters Requiring Attention (MRAs)** — for violations of Federal consumer financial law or related CMS weaknesses directly tied to violations, or
- **Supervisory Recommendations (SRs)** — for CMS weaknesses where no legal violation was identified [C:sh_issue18_2019-03_page_0018_chunk_0001]

**The evidence is insufficient to describe the specific consumer-protection or compliance findings concerning deposit accounts.** To obtain those details, the substantive deposit sections of Issues 18 and 22 would need to be included in the corpus.
